scenarios.journey: Inspect bounded Underclass stream outcomes and long-range capacity statistics
scenarios.boundary: The pinned Underclass proxy stores sanitized stream outcomes and aggregate statistics in its host-local database; the stats API, event import route and CLI require the host administrator bearer token.
scenarios.denial: Proxy-only, monitor-socket and unauthenticated callers cannot read or import statistics; prompt bodies, cache keys, credentials and unsanitized upstream error text never enter the statistics store.

scenarios.journey: Receive a served response instead of a stale 429 when a throttled Codex account recovers during the reset check
scenarios.boundary: The pinned Underclass proxy refuses with 429 and a relative Retry-After only when a fresh selection after the automatic reset attempt still finds no healthy eligible account; requests skip the reset lock while any Codex account is healthy.
scenarios.denial: When every eligible account is still cooling after the reset attempt, the request is refused with 429 and Retry-After equal to the seconds until the earliest cooling deadline; no credential or prompt enters the saturation log.

The installer validates origin, zone and host against the issued values, requires an OpenSSH client with hostname protection (9.6+), installs Microsoft.OpenSSH.Preview with winget without asking when %ProgramFiles%\OpenSSH lacks one, and with one administrator approval places %ProgramFiles%\OpenSSH before the in-box 9.5 directory in the machine PATH (resolved in the elevated process; declined elevation leaves the machine PATH unchanged and points to overalls ssh) so the machine page shows one ssh HOST command, verifies the digest, runs config-ssh --staged-installer with the downloaded binary before installing it, and connects with overalls ssh through the recorded client. The managed SSH block quotes ProxyCommand as one double-quoted absolute path because Win32-OpenSSH runs it without a shell. Updates use the same digest manifest and activate by renaming the running executable aside.

scenarios.journey: Give Windows guests an agent set with a capability table, reach a guest-side listener over virtio-vsock through the viosock driver, and make the fleet ready to stage the image
scenarios.boundary: OverallsProtocol.GuestAgents names the closed agent set (linux, none, windows-v1) and a pure capability table; Lilly's jail, driver and executor and Marshall's per-capability image facts branch on the table, never on the set's name, so the agentless none row reproduces ADR-0170 exactly. The firmware jail gets the jail-local vsock endpoint only for an agent set that speaks the Lilly protocols. The readiness budget is the agent set's (600 s for windows-v1) and is recorded once per boot. The image ships the virtio-win viosock driver and, until the real agents exist, a SYSTEM probe that discovers the provider's address family at runtime, listens on vsock port 1099 and answers the host's CONNECT with one JSON line, publishing only its own log on the EFI system partition. Windows binaries are cross-built from the shared Lyra crate with the pinned zig toolchain; the Lyra gate type-checks the library and the Windows bins for x86_64-pc-windows-gnu. Images are configured as { path } objects; a size check decides template cacheability and every root disk is copied on demand (ADR-0177); both hosts' template budget is 96 GiB.
scenarios.denial: An unknown agent set string, a workspace source version 2 on an agentless manifest or a ninth manifest key is refused by the protocol; an older Lilly refuses a windows-v1 bundle, so the converged push precedes any placement. A missing, corrupt or mismatched manifest yields every capability false in Marshall. A bare image path or any image key beyond path, including the retired standby key, refuses Lilly's configuration. The probe carries no identity or credential material. The editor and the Inception profile stay refused for windows-v1.
scenarios.scope: Protocol tests pin the capability table and the windows-v1 manifest and bundle vectors; Lilly tests pin the agentless jail configuration, the vsock addition for windows-v1, the recorded readiness budget, the image configuration shape and template cacheability; Marshall tests bind the capabilities to the exact image ID for every agent set and exercise the per-capability surfaces; the windows-guest-unit evaluation checks the viosock driver, the agents directory, the probe task, the manifest arguments and the launcher's vsock device; the lyra check builds and type-checks the Windows target. Recorded on 2026-10-14: lyraWindows built overalls-winprobe.exe (PE32+, 320 000 bytes) through zig. The windows-guest machine test dials the probe through the launcher's vsock socket after the SAC prompt and reads its published log. The agents composition now also inspects the live Windows EFI log for the closed agentd startup line; this is present evidence only until the composed check runs. The current sealed e9ed22f1 image in live run 075200 reported ready while sshd was stopped and CLI SSH failed; that current failure is distinct from earlier dated fleet proofs.
scenarios.gaps: Fleet proofs on 2026-10-15 cover creation to ready in seconds, trust, roster accounts and sshd, the host certificate, executor registration, a public workspace clone and a relocation between hosts (review). Still unproven: an SSH login through Audi, a roster-user ConPTY terminal under an S4U logon and an agent turn (they need a browser-approved key), crash restart of the scheduled-task agents, the pool-level refill with an uncacheable image configured, and no Marshall-driven Windows fleet test makes any of the fleet proofs repeatable; ConPTY re-renders terminal output.
scenarios.preferred_gap: Record the browser-approved proofs (SSH through Audi, a roster-user terminal, an agent turn) and add a Marshall-driven Windows fleet test so the fleet proofs become machine tests.

scenarios.journey: Place the Windows image through Lilly as a guest without agents and reach it on its delivered /32
scenarios.boundary: The protocol admits exactly the eight-key version-5 manifest and the seven-key version-2 firmware bundle beside the unchanged version-4 and version-1 shapes; artifact names come from the protocol only. Lilly's host policy drops every unmarked packet between the host and a Customer guest, so nothing on the host reaches the Windows guest except the SSH and editor ingress paths it does not yet have.
